title: Security & Compliance: RBAC, Audit Logging, Data Residency, SDLC, Incident Response, Evidence & Exceptions
author: Aisha Patel
content:
### Overview

This document consolidates Redwood Inference's security and compliance controls and operational procedures for: RBAC & authentication, audit logging, data residency & retention, secure SDLC requirements, incident response security procedures, compliance evidence workflows, and risk & exceptions. It is intended for engineers, SRE, security, and compliance reviewers who implement or operate services that handle customer data or run on Redwood's infrastructure.

### Scope

Applies to: All Redwood services (hosted, dedicated control plane, and private deployment control plane) and supporting infrastructure (CI/CD, logging/observability, identity providers).

Excludes: Customer-managed on-prem components that are explicitly out-of-scope per contract.

---

### Ownership & Contacts

- Document owner: Security Operations (security-infra@redwood.ai)
- Primary contact: Aisha Patel (Director, Security)
- On-call contacts: sec-oncall@redwood.ai

### Principles

- Least privilege by default across all services and infrastructure
- Authentication and strong MFA for human and machine identities
- Immutable, auditable evidence for configuration and access
- Deterministic retention and data residency aligned with contract requirements
- Security gating in the SDLC to prevent regressions

---

### RBAC & Authentication

Summary:
- All human users authenticate via company SSO (SAML/OIDC) with mandatory MFA (TOTP or hardware keys).
- Machine identities use short-lived workload identities (OIDC tokens) or KMS-backed service principals.
- Resource access is enforced via centralized RBAC policies defined in the access-control service (accessctl).

Role definitions (examples):
1. admin: full control for platform admins; granted sparingly (max 6 active across company)
2. infra-operator: manage infra components (deployment, scaling) but no customer data access
3. se: solutions engineer; scoped customer-support access with time-bound approvals
4. auditor: read-only access to logs, metrics, and audit evidence

Implementation details:
- Access policies are stored as YAML in git (gitops) in repo: infra/access-policies.
- Changes require PR with two approvers from security or infrastructure teams and CI policy checks.
- Example policy snippet:

```yaml
- role: se
  resources:
    - namespace: customer-support/*
  permissions:
    - read:logs
    - create:ephemeral-ssh
  max_duration: 2h
```

- Privileged sessions (break-glass) must be requested via the access portal (https://access.redwood.ai), logged, and require post-approval within 24 hours.
- Service accounts rotate credentials every 24 hours and use KMS to encrypt secrets in transit and at rest.

SLOs & thresholds:
- Access policy PR review time target: <= 24h for normal requests
- Privileged access alerting: immediate Slack + PagerDuty for any break-glass activation

---

### Audit Logging

What we log (minimum):
- Authentication events (success/failure, MFA events)
- Authorization decisions (policy evals, RBAC grants/revokes)
- Administrative actions (role changes, policy updates)
- Data access events (store/retrieve/delete operations on customer data)
- CI/CD actions (deployments, artifact promotions)

Logging pipeline:
1. Services emit structured JSON events to stdout or to in-cluster logging agent (fluentd).
2. Logs are forwarded to centralized logging cluster (ELK/Opensearch) with immutable write-once indices per retention policy.
3. Critical events are forwarded to SIEM (Splunk) for correlation and alerting.

Operational requirements:
- Audit log ingestion latency: peak <= 2 minutes, 99th percentile <= 30s
- Log integrity: logs are signed and checksummed via KMS-based signing on ingestion
- Log storage: encrypted at rest (AES-256) with KMS keys per-region

Retention & access:
- Default audit log retention: 365 days in hot indices, 2 years in cold storage (configurable per customer contract)
- Auditor role provides read-only access; export requires approval and is recorded as a data export event

Example retrieval (CLI):

```bash
aws s3 cp s3://redwood-logs-prod/audit/2026/05/12/part-000.json - | jq '. | select(.event_type=="auth_failure")'
```

---

### Data Residency & Retention

Residency controls:
- Customer data is tagged at creation with residency attributes (region: us-east-1, eu-west-1, ap-southeast-1).
- Data is stored only in approved regions per customer contract; cross-region replication requires explicit legal and security approval.

Retention matrix (example):
- Customer request data (text inputs): default retention 30 days (hosted API), configurable up to 7 years for enterprise
- Audit logs: default 365 days hot, 2 years cold
- Backups & snapshots: 90 days

Data deletion process:
1. Deletion requests are enqueued in deletion service and processed asynchronously
2. Steps: mark data -> remove replicas -> scrub object storage -> zero-out indexes (where feasible)
3. Verify deletion via hash-based proof-of-deletion stored in audit index

Regulatory mappings:
- GDPR: data subject access/erasure requests handled within 30 days
- CCPA: comply with consumer requests per policy
- Export controls: restrict model weights/PKI material per export-control policy

---

### Secure SDLC Requirements

Must-have controls for all repos/services:
- Protected branches with required reviews (2 approvers for infrastructure, 1 for application code)
- Mandatory CI gates:
  - Unit and integration tests
  - Static analysis (semgrep/ghas)
  - Dependency scanning (Snyk/OSS scanners) blocking for high/critical libs
  - Secrets scanning (truffleHog/Detect-secrets) failing on secrets
- Artifact signing: all release artifacts must be signed (sigstore) prior to deployment
- Canary deployments with automatic rollback on error budget breaches

Developer checklist (pre-merge):
1. Add unit tests covering new logic
2. Run 'make format && make lint' locally
3. Ensure no new high-risk dependencies
4. Attach threat-model notes for changes touching auth/data paths

---

### Incident Response — Security Procedures

Objective: preserve evidence, restore service, and communicate with stakeholders while minimizing customer impact.

Incident classification:
- Sev1 (Data breach / service down affecting >10% customers)
- Sev2 (Elevated risk, limited customer impact)
- Sev3 (Low-impact anomaly)

Immediate steps (first 60 minutes):
1. Triage: identify scope, services, and affected region(s) (owner: oncall-sre)
2. Containment: apply ACLs, rotate affected keys, isolate pods or nodes
3. Evidence preservation: snapshot relevant volumes, export logs (preserve original timestamps), preserve memory dumps if applicable
4. Notification: open incident in incident system and notify security-oncall and product leads

Forensics & evidence handling:
- All preserved artifacts are stored in a write-once evidence bucket: s3://redwood-evidence/<incident-id>/
- Each artifact must include metadata: collected_by, collection_time_utc, collection_command, sha256
- Use forensic playbooks for memory/image analysis; chain-of-custody log is maintained for any external sharing

Post-incident:
- Postmortem within 7 business days for Sev1/Sev2 incidents, including root cause, impact, remediation, and preventive measures
- Compliance notification obligations (customers, regulators) executed per legal template and timelines

---

### Compliance Evidence Workflows

Automation & packaging:
- Evidence collection is automated via compliance-runner (CI job) that exports artifacts into a per-audit evidence bundle (ZIP) with manifest.json
- Evidence manifest fields: artifact_name, path, sha256, generated_at, owner

Audit cadence & owners:
- SOC2 Type 2 annual audit owner: Head of Compliance (compliance@redwood.ai)
- Quarterly internal control reviews: control owners listed in control registry (infra/security/product)

On-demand evidence requests (process):
1. Request submitted to compliance@redwood.ai with audit_id and scope
2. Compliance owner validates scope and issues a signed download link
3. All access to evidence bundles is logged and requires 2-factor approval for sensitive bundles

Retention & versioning:
- Evidence bundles retained for 7 years
- Internal change logs to evidence are versioned in compliance-evidence repo

Example command to generate a bundle:

```bash
make generate-evidence AUDIT_ID=SOC2-2026-RED
aws s3 cp artifacts/${AUDIT_ID}.zip s3://redwood-compliance-evidence/ --sse aws:kms
```

---

### Risk & Exceptions

Exception lifecycle:
1. Submit request via exception-tracker (jira template: "SEC-EXCEPTION") with compensating controls and TTL
2. Security reviews and records compensating controls; high-risk exceptions require CISO approval and exec sponsor
3. Exceptions are time-bound (default 90 days) and automatically escalated if not remediated

Exception template fields (required):
- title
- affected_systems
- risk_impact
- compensating_controls
- mitigation_plan
- owner
- ttl

Monitoring & remediation:
- Exceptions trigger a weekly report to leadership and monthly remediation reviews
- Technical debt linked to exceptions assigned to engineering squads and prioritized in quarterly planning
